transcript: When you're in danger or extreme excitement, your brain sends a signal to your adrenal glands. They release adrenaline, also known as epinephrine, straight into your bloodstream. Your heart rate spikes. Your airways open. Blood flows to your muscles. Pupils dilate. Suddenly, you're stronger, faster, more alert. This is the fight-or-flight response built into us for survival. It's what lets a mother lift a car to save her child. or a base jumper leap off a cliff without hesitation. Adrenaline doesn't just protect, it pushes your limits. So next time you feel that rush, don't panic. That's evolution giving you a boost. Feel the thrill. Embrace the power. That's adrenaline.
metadata_caption:
Adrenaline Rush: Why Your Body Loves the Thrill!



Ever wondered why your heart races when you're scared or excited? That’s adrenaline kicking in! In this 1-minute video, we’ll dive into how adrenaline works, why it gives you superhuman strength, and how it can literally save your life. Perfect for thrill-seekers, science lovers, and anyone curious about the power of our own bodies!
